strengths: WMDD addresses an important practical problem with a clear, modular combination of feature distribution compression and per-class BatchNorm regularization.
The reported results are strong at moderate compression budgets. At 50 images per class, WMDD achieves 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus CDA's 53.5%, and 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus 48.7% (Table 1).

The evaluation includes multiple datasets, image budgets, cross-architecture transfer, and component and hyperparameter ablations. Table 4 supports the complementary value of feature matching and per-class regularization.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, training hyperparameters, and a code link, and generally attributes its datasets and underlying methods appropriately. The supplementary discussion acknowledges inherited dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central formulation needs clearer positioning. For a single empirical distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized atom weights, the objective in Section 4 is exactly k-means/vector quantization: each real feature can assign its mass to its nearest prototype. This equivalence should be acknowledged, with a centroid-based feature inversion baseline using the same PCBN/FKD pipeline. The multiple-distribution barycenter illustration does not establish additional benefits for this setting.

The headline improvements are insufficiently attributed. On ImageNet-1K at 10 IPC, the CE+BN control achieves 35.9% in Table 4, whereas SRe2L achieves 21.3% in Table 1. This large discrepancy needs reconciliation through matched training recipes and an ablation of learned sample weights. With PCBN fixed, the Wasserstein feature objective contributes a smaller, although meaningful, 1.7-point improvement.

The MMD comparison does not isolate the distance metric: Section 5.6 retains differences between pretrained and randomly initialized feature extractors. At 1 IPC, the proposed squared-Wasserstein barycenter is simply the feature mean, making Equation 12 equivalent to linear-MMD mean matching under the same encoder. Consequently, the near-random MMD result cannot establish the claimed geometric explanation. Appendix B's generic risk bounds do not resolve this experimental confound.

The optimization description has unresolved correctness and reproducibility details. Algorithm 2 updates the weights but reuses a transport plan computed with the previous marginals for its position update. Simplex projection can also produce zero weights, making the stated inverse-Hessian update undefined. The barycenter initialization, step size, and precise use of weights during FKD are unspecified. These may be correctable omissions, but the implemented procedure needs clarification.

The efficiency evidence is narrower than the scalability claims. Table 3 compares methods only on ImageNette at 1 IPC, where barycenter computation reduces to a mean. Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings, but comparative ImageNet-1K time and memory measurements, with clearly defined accounting for pretraining, feature extraction, and relabeling, are missing.
